faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Platform questions, *answered*
faq.text: What CIOs, CISOs and business owners ask most before a demo.
items: Do we have to replace our ERP, CRM or data warehouse?
No. The platform connects to the systems you already run, read-only by default, and builds the organization model on top of them. Your systems remain the source of truth.
Is our data used to train AI models?

No. Frontier models are used through enterprise APIs whose terms exclude training on your data, and personal data is masked before it leaves. Sovereign models are fine-tuned on your corpus inside your perimeter and are not shared with anyone.
Can the platform run fully on-premises or air-gapped?

Yes. On-premises takes 2–4 weeks to deploy and air-gapped 4–8 weeks, depending on your infrastructure. In an air-gapped network the platform runs on local models only, with no internet access. GPU hardware is priced separately.
Which language models do you use?

Frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic and other leading providers, and open models such as Llama, Qwen and Mistral running locally. The platform is model-agnostic, so a model can be swapped without rebuilding the solution.
How do you stop agents from making things up?

Every answer must link to a record or document. When data is insufficient, the agent says so. Each agent is tested against a reference set of real questions before release and before every update, and actions that change data need human approval.
How long does it take to connect a system?

A system with a documented API or database replica is usually connected within the pilot. Undocumented legacy databases and paper archives take longer and are scoped during the [diagnostic](/approach).
Which regulations does the platform support?

We design deployments to support compliance with the GDPR and the EU AI Act, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD, PIPL, APPI, PIPA, the Australian Privacy Act and sector rules such as HIPAA-style health data requirements. Data residency is solved by the deployment option. Details on the [security page](/security).
Can our own systems call the agents?
Yes. The platform API lets your applications send a task to an agent and receive the result with its sources, under the same permissions and audit log as any user.
What does the platform cost?

It is licensed as an annual package: Foundation at {foundation}, Enterprise at {enterprise} and Sovereign at {sovereign} per year. A diagnostic ({diagnostic}, credited to the pilot) and a pilot come first. See [pricing](/pricing#packages).
What do you need from our IT team?
Read-only access to the agreed sources, a technical contact, network access for the deployment and help setting up single sign-on. Our forward-deployed engineers do the integration work.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Questions about *the method*
items: What is a forward-deployed engineer?

A software engineer who works inside your organization, next to the people who do the work. They map the process, connect systems, configure agents and stay accountable for the result. It is the opposite of a consultant who writes a report and a separate team that builds something else.
How long until we see a working result?
Usually about eleven weeks: a diagnostic of 2–3 weeks and a pilot of 4–8 weeks. You see working software on your own data at the weekly demos from around week five.
What does the diagnostic cost, and what if we stop after it?

The diagnostic costs {diagnostic} and is credited to the pilot if you continue. If you stop, you keep the opportunity map and ROI estimate. They are written so another vendor or your own team could act on them.
How much of our staff's time does it take?

The process owner spends 2–4 hours a week, IT a few hours to grant access, and the pilot group of 5–20 users works with the solution on real tasks in the second half of the pilot. The sponsor attends the steering committee every 2–4 weeks.
Do your engineers need to be on site the whole time?

No. They are on site for kick-off, interviews, launch and acceptance, and for longer periods in Enterprise and Sovereign engagements. Air-gapped work is always done on your premises. The rest runs remotely in your business hours.
Can you work in Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific?

Yes. Engineers travel to the client for on-site phases, and the remote cadence is scheduled inside your working day. Deployment can stay in your region or on your own infrastructure to meet data-residency rules; see [security](/security).
How do you prove the impact?
By measuring a baseline before anything changes and the same metric after launch, with the method written down at the start. The process owner co-signs the numbers in the pilot report.
Who owns what you build?
Your data, agent instructions, process documentation and reports stay yours. The platform is licensed through an annual package; details are in the contract and on the [pricing page](/pricing).
What happens after the pilot?

If the pilot meets its acceptance criteria, integration takes 2–4 months within the first subscription year: all required systems, single sign-on, training and handover to SLA support. Then we add processes one by one.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Questions about *use cases*
items: Which use case should we start with?

The one that happens every day, has data, can be measured and has an owner who wants it changed. The diagnostic scores 3–5 candidates on exactly these points and recommends one; see [how we choose](/solutions#pilot).
Our problem isn't on this page. Can you still solve it?

Probably. The library shows what we see most often, not everything we do. If the work involves reading, checking, routing or reporting on information in your systems, it is usually a fit. Describe it in a [request](/contact) and an engineer will answer.
Do we need clean, centralized data before we start?

No. Most clients start with data spread across an ERP, spreadsheets and mailboxes. The platform connects to where it lives. If records are missing entirely, we say so in the diagnostic and recommend fixing record-keeping first.
Which systems can you connect?

ERP and accounting systems such as SAP, Oracle and Microsoft Dynamics, CRMs such as Salesforce, document stores, mail, telephony, databases, spreadsheets and cameras. If a system has an API, a database replica or a file export, we can usually connect it.
How quickly does a use case pay back?
We don't promise a number before the diagnostic. It produces an ROI estimate with a conservative and an expected case for your process, and the pilot measures the real result against a baseline.
Will the AI make decisions on its own?
Only where you allow it. By default agents prepare and propose; a person approves actions above {threshold} or when the agent is not confident. Every step is logged.
Is our data used to train AI models?
No. Cloud models are used through enterprise APIs whose terms exclude training on customer data, and local models run inside your infrastructure. See [security](/security).
Do you work with government and regulated industries?
Yes. Public bodies, banks, energy companies and healthcare administrators usually choose on-premises or air-gapped deployment with local models. See [AI for government](/government).
Which languages do the agents work in?
Text agents work in all major languages. Voice agents support English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, among others.

jur.label: Jurisdictions
jur.title: Built for the rules of *your* jurisdiction
jur.text: Public bodies answer to stricter rules than companies. Below is what typically matters in each region and how the platform is designed to support it. Your legal team and data-protection officer make the final assessment; we provide the technical documentation they need.
jur.needLabel: What it means for public bodies
jur.howLabel: How we design to support it

items.need: Lawful basis and data minimization, a DPIA for high-risk processing, processor agreements. Under the EU AI Act, public deployers of high-risk systems — for example in access to public services and benefits — must ensure human oversight, keep logs and, for bodies governed by public law, carry out a fundamental-rights impact assessment. People must be told when they talk to an AI.
items.how: Processing in EU infrastructure or on your premises, human sign-off enforced by the platform, full logs, AI disclosure in citizen channels, and a documentation pack for your DPIA and fundamental-rights assessment.

items.need: Federal agencies follow government-wide AI governance guidance: inventories of AI use, risk management for rights- and safety-impacting uses, and accountable officials. States and cities add their own privacy, records and AI rules. Cloud services may require an authorization you already hold.
items.how: Deployment inside your authorized environment — your data center or your accredited cloud tenant. Risk documentation mapped to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, records exportable for retention schedules, and human review for any rights-impacting output.

items.need: LGPD has a dedicated chapter for public authorities: processing must serve a public purpose, be transparent and be reported. The regulator can request a data-protection impact report. Other Latin American countries have their own data-protection laws with similar principles.
items.how: In-country deployment, a processing record per use case, Portuguese and Spanish interfaces and speech, and documentation that supports your impact report and your data-protection officer.

items.need: Since the recent amendments, APPI also covers national administrative organs and local governments. Agencies need clear purposes of use, security controls and care with transfers abroad. Cloud procurement may require registered services.
items.how: On-premises or in your approved Japanese cloud environment, local models with native Japanese handling, purpose and access recorded per agent, and no transfer of personal data abroad in sovereign deployments.

items.need: PIPA sets strict rules for public institutions on purpose limitation, safety measures and cross-border transfer. Public-sector cloud use is subject to its own security assurance regime.
items.how: On-premises or air-gapped deployment, Korean-language models and speech, field-level access control and a complete access log that supports your PIPA safety-measure obligations.

items.need: PIPL and the Data Security Law restrict cross-border transfer and require localization of personal information and important data for many operators. Public-facing generative AI services fall under the 2023 interim measures, which can require filing.
items.how: Deployment inside mainland China on local models only — no calls to foreign model APIs. Data, logs and keys stay in-country, and we provide technical documentation to support your filings.

laws: Policy for responsible AI in government
items.need: Commonwealth agencies apply the Australian Privacy Principles and the whole-of-government policy for responsible AI use, which asks for accountable officials and public transparency statements. States and territories add their own privacy laws and security frameworks.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Questions public-sector buyers *ask*
items: Can the platform run with no internet connection at all?

Yes. In the air-gapped setup, models, agents, the knowledge index and the audit log run inside your network with no route out. Updates arrive as signed offline packages. Frontier cloud models are not available in that mode; local models tuned on your corpus take their place.
Is the platform compliant with GDPR, the EU AI Act or our national law?

We design the platform to support compliance — in-country processing, human oversight, logging, access control and deletion — and we provide documentation for your DPIA or impact assessment. We do not certify compliance; the legal assessment stays with your organization and its data-protection officer.
Will AI make decisions about citizens?

No. The agent classifies, drafts and checks. Decisions on benefits, permits, sanctions and any legally binding act are taken and signed by the responsible official. The platform enforces this through roles and approvals; it is not left to good intentions.
Do you hold FedRAMP, IRAP, ISMAP or similar authorizations?

No. We deploy into the environment you have already accredited — your data center or your authorized cloud tenant — and support your assessment with architecture documents, a threat model, a completed questionnaire and cooperation with your penetration testers. See [Security](/security).
How long from first meeting to a working pilot?
The diagnostic takes 2–3 weeks and the pilot 4–8 weeks. Procurement time depends on your rules, which is why many agencies start with a pilot that fits their own approval limits.
Which languages are supported?

Eight interface and answer languages out of the box: English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese and Korean. Others are added per project, including speech recognition and synthesis tuned on your real requests.
How do we avoid vendor lock-in?

The platform runs on your infrastructure, models can be swapped, and data, prompts, configurations and logs are exportable in open formats. Models fine-tuned on your corpus stay in your environment; ownership terms are fixed in the contract. Your team receives documentation and training throughout.
What happens to our data when the contract ends?
Data is deleted within the agreed period and we issue a deletion certificate. In on-premises and air-gapped setups the data never leaves your servers in the first place.
Where is BlackGust based, and can you work on site?
BlackGust is headquartered in Tashkent. Our forward-deployed engineers work on site with your team at the phases that need it and, in the Sovereign package, as a dedicated embedded team.
What does it cost?

A diagnostic costs {diagnostic} and is credited to the pilot; pilots start from {pilot}. Organization-wide sovereign work is covered by the Sovereign package at {sovereign}/year, with GPU hardware priced separately. Details are on the [pricing page](/pricing#compare).

items: Do you use our data to train models?

No. Frontier models are accessed through enterprise APIs whose terms exclude training on customer data. Local models run inside your infrastructure. Fine-tuning on your corpus happens only in your environment, at your request.
Do you hold SOC 2 or ISO 27001?

No. We say so openly. To compensate, we deploy in environments you control — private cloud, on-premises or air-gapped — and give your team the architecture, threat model, completed questionnaire and access to our engineers, plus cooperation with your penetration test.
Can we hold the encryption keys?

Yes, in private-cloud, on-premises and air-gapped deployments the keys stay in your key management service or HSM. In BlackGust Cloud, keys are managed by BlackGust in the same region; if you must hold them yourself, choose one of the other modes.
Can we run a penetration test?
Yes. We agree scope and timing, your testers or your chosen firm test the pilot environment, we fix findings and support the retest.
How do you stop prompt injection?

We assume it will be attempted. Retrieved content is treated as data, not instructions; inputs are filtered; and, most importantly, agents cannot exceed the user's rights or take risky actions without human approval. A successful injection hits the same walls as any user.
How quickly will you tell us about an incident?

Without undue delay, within the timeline fixed in the contract so you can meet your own regulatory deadlines. In the Sovereign package, critical incidents get a 1-hour response from a named duty engineer.
Which subprocessors are involved?

It depends on the mode. With frontier models, the model provider's enterprise API is a subprocessor; in BlackGust Cloud, so is the hosting provider in your region. In on-premises and air-gapped deployments without frontier models, there are none. The full list is in the DPA.
Can BlackGust engineers see production data?
Only named engineers, for the agreed period, with logged access that is revoked at handover. In air-gapped deployments they work on site under your supervision and access rules.
Can logs go to our SIEM?
Yes. The audit log exports to your SIEM in standard formats, and retention follows your policy. SIEM export is part of the Enterprise and Sovereign packages.

items: How much does BlackGust cost?

The platform is an annual subscription: Foundation {foundation}, Enterprise {enterprise}, Sovereign {sovereign} per year. Before it you pay for a diagnostic ({diagnostic}, credited toward the pilot) and a fixed-price pilot from {pilot}. The first consultation is free.
Why an annual subscription and not per user or per token?

Because the value comes from connecting the organization and keeping engineers on the process, not from seats. A fixed annual price is easier to budget and procure, and it doesn't punish you for adoption.
Which package do most organizations choose?

Most start with a pilot, then sign Enterprise once two or three departments want in. Foundation fits a single function or a first business case. Sovereign is for governments, critical infrastructure and groups that require on-premises or air-gapped deployment.
Are engineers included in the price?
Yes. Forward-deployed engineers are part of every package: one lead in Foundation, a team of three in Enterprise, an embedded team of five or more with an architect in Sovereign.
What isn't included?

GPU servers and infrastructure for on-premises or air-gapped deployments, model usage above the agreed allowance, your existing vendors' license fees, and add-on modules. All of these are stated in the proposal before you sign.
Can we start small and grow?

Yes. All packages run on the same platform and the same organization model, so moving from Foundation to Enterprise or Sovereign extends what's built. Unused value is credited when you upgrade mid-term.
Do prices differ by country?
No separate regional price lists. Prices are in USD, or EUR for clients in Europe. Taxes, travel beyond the package and local legal review are stated in the proposal.
How do government bodies buy it?
Through a pilot, a competitive tender or a direct contract where procurement rules allow. The Sovereign package includes a procurement-ready documentation package. See [Government](/government).

groups.title: General
items: What is BlackGust, in plain terms?

A platform plus a team of engineers. The platform links data from your systems into one picture and gives AI agents safe access to it. The engineers embed that into the work of specific departments, from leadership questions to document processing.
How is this different from a ChatGPT chatbot?

A chatbot knows what's on the internet. Our agents work with your data — contracts, accounting, CRM — within the user's permissions, cite their sources and can take actions inside your processes. On top of that: audit logs, controls, and deployment in your jurisdiction or on your servers.
Do you sell a product or services?
Both. The platform is the foundation the solution is built on. Our engineers' work is what makes it useful for your organization specifically. We don't sell the license on its own without delivery.
Who are your clients?
Large enterprises, state enterprises and government bodies. The platform is built for organizations with many departments, systems and people.
Which regions do you work in?
Europe, North and South America, China, Japan, Korea and Australia. Our engineers travel to the client for the diagnostic and key phases, and we schedule calls in your time zone.
How are BlackGust and AISolution related?
BlackGust is the international brand of [AISolution](/aisolution). Same team, same platform, same accountability.

groups.title: Founder & CEO
items: What impact can we expect?

It depends on the process. Typical outcomes: routine operations take a fraction of the time, leadership questions are answered in seconds instead of days, and fewer losses come from missed deadlines. The diagnostic gives a concrete estimate for your organization, built on your numbers.
How long until the first result?
An opportunity map with estimates in 2–3 weeks. A working pilot on one process 4–8 weeks after the diagnostic.
What if it doesn't work?
The project is split into phases with separate acceptance. Your minimum exposure is the cost of the diagnostic, {diagnostic}. If we don't find a process with measurable impact, we say so.
Why not build this with our own IT team?

You can, if your team has experience with language models, agents, local-language speech and AI quality evaluation. It's usually faster to start with us and train your engineers in parallel; knowledge transfer is part of every engagement.
Will we become dependent on you?
We design to keep dependency low: documentation, configuration access, training for your engineers. Models can be swapped, and the data stays with you.
Who will work on our project?
A lead engineer who runs the project from diagnostic to launch, plus a team sized to the task. You'll know their names and experience before we start.

groups.title: Finance
items: How much does it cost?

The consultation is free. The diagnostic is {diagnostic} (credited toward the pilot), pilots start at {pilot}. The platform is an annual subscription in three packages: Foundation {foundation}, Enterprise {enterprise} and Sovereign {sovereign} per year, engineers included. See [pricing](/pricing).
What currency do you invoice in?
We invoice at fixed list prices in USD or EUR, as shown on the site. Another currency can be agreed in the contract.
What does the subscription include?
The platform and the modules in scope, forward-deployed engineers, integration of your systems, model usage under the agreed plan, SLA support and quarterly impact reviews.
How is acceptance handled?
Each phase ends with a report, a demo and a signed acceptance certificate. Payment is by milestone.
How do you calculate payback?
We record baseline process metrics (time, volume, errors, losses) and measure the same metrics after the pilot. The difference in money, minus support and model costs, is the monthly impact.

groups.title: IT
items: Do we need to change our systems?
No. We connect to existing systems through APIs, database replicas or exports. Access is read-only by default.
Which systems do you integrate with?

ERP (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics), CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics), databases and warehouses (PostgreSQL, Oracle, MS SQL, Snowflake, BigQuery), Kafka, document management, email, VoIP telephony, Teams, Slack, CCTV. Anything non-standard is assessed during the audit.
Where is the platform deployed?
In BlackGust Cloud, your private cloud, your own servers, or an air-gapped network. See [Deployment](/platform#deploy).
What servers do local models need?
It depends on load and the models chosen. Air-gapped deployments usually need GPU servers. We prepare the spec during the diagnostic.
How do users sign in?
Through your directory: Active Directory / LDAP, SAML or OIDC. Roles and groups are inherited.
Who supports the solution after launch?
We do, under an SLA. We also train your engineers and hand over documentation so you can make some changes yourselves.

groups.title: Security
items: Are models trained on our data?
No. Cloud models are accessed through enterprise APIs that don't train on customer data; local models run inside your infrastructure.
Do you meet data-residency requirements?

Yes. Personal data is stored and processed in the jurisdiction its law requires: in the EU under GDPR, in China under PIPL, in Japan under APPI, in Korea under PIPA, in Brazil under LGPD, in Australia under the Privacy Act.
Can an agent do something without a human knowing?
Only what its configuration explicitly allows. Changing data, sending documents outside and legally binding actions all require human approval.
Can we review documentation before signing?
Yes. Under NDA we provide an architecture description and threat model, and we complete your security questionnaire. See [Security](/security).

groups.title: Department head
items: How much of my team's time will this take?
The process owner spends 2–4 hours a week during the pilot. Everyone else joins interviews and testing, 1–2 hours each.
Will AI replace my staff?
The goal is to remove routine so people can focus on work that needs their expertise. Decisions and approvals stay with people.
What if the AI gets something wrong?
Every answer links to its source, so errors are easy to check. Where mistakes are costly, a human approves. Errors we find are added to the reference tests so they don't recur.
Can we change agent instructions without a developer?
Yes. Instructions and rules are configured in the interface, and we train a designated person on your team to do it.

groups.title: Government & procurement
items: How can a government body contract with you?
Through a pilot project, a competitive tender, or a direct contract where procurement rules allow. We help prepare the specification and documentation.
Can it run without internet access?
Yes, in an air-gapped environment on local language models.
Can models be trained on our own data?
Yes. In a sovereign deployment, open models are fine-tuned on your documents and terminology inside your perimeter. Neither the data nor the trained weights leave your infrastructure.
Which languages are supported?
English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese and Korean for the interface and agent answers. Speech is configured and quality-checked per project, and other languages can be added.
What documents do you hand over?
Project schedule, test program and methodology, user and administrator guides, and a report for each phase. See [Government](/government).

groups.title: Staff

Wherever is convenient: in the web interface, in Teams or Slack, or by voice. There's no complex new software to learn.
Is there training?
Yes, on real tasks, by role, in the team's language. Plus short guides and a contact for questions.
Can the system read my personal messages?
No. Only sources agreed with the organization and its security team are connected, and every data access is logged.

faq.title: Questions about *AISolution*
items: Is BlackGust a separate company?
BlackGust is the international brand of AISolution: the same team, platform and method. The contracting party for your project is stated in the proposal.
Is BlackGust an OpenAI partner too?
The OpenAI Select Partner status belongs to AISolution. BlackGust projects are delivered by the same AISolution team.
Will the same engineers work on my project?
Yes. One team serves both brands. The engineers who deliver in Uzbekistan are the ones who come on site for your diagnostic and key phases.
We operate in Uzbekistan. Whom should we contact?
AISolution, at [aisolution.uz](https://aisolution.uz): contracts and payment in soums, work in Russian and Uzbek.
Where is the team based?

In Tashkent, Uzbekistan. Forward-deployed engineers come on site for the diagnostic and key phases; the rest of the work runs remotely, inside the deployment you choose. See [our approach](/approach).
Can we see AISolution's work?

The [AISolution website](https://aisolution.uz) and its blog describe its products and projects. We name clients only with their consent; ask for references during the diagnostic and we share them where clients agree.
